Lena P: FYI automated audit flagged a batch of database snapshot uploads with missing SSE-C headers for org=tenant-11 between 2026-04-02T04:10:00Z and 04:22:00Z. Not sure if this is a policy drift or an agent regression.

deploybot: policy-audit: s3-sse-check failure count=6 bucket=redwood-snapshots-prod prefix=tenant-11/ :warning:

Ravi S: Uh. Any recent IAM changes? I pushed a narrow role change to `snapshot-uploader` yesterday to remove an overly-broad assume-role that a vendor used. Did that coincide?

Lena P: I made a minor IAM change at 2026-04-02T03:58Z: removed the assume-role permission for `vendor/proxy` on the uploader role. Intended to harden access.

Theo G: Could be related. Quick KMS audit: I see a GrantRevoke for CMK arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456:key/zxy-123 at 04:01:05Z referencing principal arn:aws:iam::999999:role/vendor-proxy. Also a GrantCreate for remediation-service at 04:12:30Z.

Nadia M: Head-object for one of the suspect uploads:
```
aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-snapshots-prod --key tenant-11/20260402-db-snap-1.tar.gz
```
response excerpt: `{"ContentLength": 98765432, "Metadata": {}}` — no sse metadata and metadata.encrypted missing.

Ravi S: This smells like the uploader agent's fail-open behavior again: if it cannot acquire ephemeral grant it falls back to uploading without SSE rather than blocking. Did we roll an agent change?

Theo G: CI shows a canary rollout of uploader agent v2.3.4 that includes an SSE fallback fix was started at 03:45Z but was paused at 04:05Z due to a health alert. Some hosts may be halfway through the rollout.

encops-bot: incident-created id=INC-20260402-DBSNAP-1 severity=medium assignees=eng-security,eng-sre

Lena P: Containment suggestions: 1) Block further uploads with missing SSE via S3 bucket policy (deny PutObject without x-amz-server-side-encryption header) for that prefix; 2) Revoke read/restore on the suspect objects; 3) Snapshot the objects off-line for investigation. Any objections?

Ravi S: Bucket policy change is heavy-handed but effective. We must coordinate with support because it will break any legitimate third-party uploads. If vendors rely on assume-role, we'll need to thaw after remediation.

Theo G: Before policy change, can we run a quick inventory scan for objects with no SSE and tag them `needs-reencrypt=true`? I can spin up a lambda to list-objects-v2 and head-object each key.

Nadia M: Doing that now. Also capturing audit trail: CloudTrail shows IAMPolicyChange by lena@redwood at 03:58:43Z and a KMS GrantRevoke at 04:01:05Z by kms-admin. I'm storing the CloudTrail event IDs in the case file.

Ravi S: For remediation plan: two options — (A) restore a short-lived grant to a remediation role and re-encrypt+rewrite objects OR (B) download raw objects to a locked remediation bucket (encrypted by us) and then replace originals. Option A preferred if we can safely create a limited grant.

Lena P: Agreement: create grant for `remediate-snap` role with TTL 30m, key policy restrict to single account actions, log every KMS Encrypt/Decrypt. Approving now.

encops-bot: task-created TSK-20260402-9 "inventory and re-encrypt tenant-11 unencrypted snaps" assignees=Theo G,due=2026-04-03T10:00:00Z

Theo G: Inventory complete: 6 objects found. I have object keys and sizes saved to the incident bundle. Starting re-encrypt job using remediation role. Plan: get object via GetObject, call KMS Encrypt with our CMK, PutObject with SSE-KMS header. All operations logged.

Nadia M: Forensics note: capture uploader host instance-ids that performed uploads in the window. I see 2 EC2 instances still on old agent v1.6.1. I'm creating EBS snapshots of those instances and collecting /var/log/uploader logs.

Ravi S: Filing a security bug: uploader must never write a snapshot without SSE — it should queue and fail if grants unavailable. Adding repro steps: revoke grant in staging and assert agent blocks upload. Owner: eng-runtime.

Lena P: Postmortem action items (assign owners): - enforce preflight CMK healthcheck in deploy pipeline (eng-infra) - add bucket-level deny policy template for tenant prefixes where required (eng-sre) - panic-button rollback plan for IAM changes (eng-security) - update runbooks to create temporary remediation grants (encops)

Theo G: One operational caveat: objects re-encrypted will change ETag; replication and restore references must be updated. We need to notify backup-indexing that keys changed.

encops-bot: incident-resolved INC-20260402-DBSNAP-1 resolution=remediated notes="temporary grant issued, 6 objects re-encrypted, two old agents decommissioned, bucket policy deferred" closed_by=lena@redwood

Lena P: Thanks team. We'll schedule a follow-up postmortem doc and include timeline, root cause (partial rollout + grant revoke + fail-open agent), and remediation. :memo:
